leads.title: Indigo dyeing in West Africa
leads.where: Bandiagara escarpment, Mali, and the West African savanna and forest
leads.why: Indigo cloth became the staple prestige textile and a major trade good across West Africa, with large dye-pit industries from Kano to Yorubaland.
leads.verify: Find the earliest dated indigo-dyed textiles in West Africa (the Tellem cave textiles are the usual reference) and any earlier evidence. Establish whether the use of local Philenoptera (Lonchocarpus) cyanescens points to a local invention or to knowledge arriving across the Sahara with cotton.

leads.title: Coal-tar aniline dyes in London
leads.why: Mauveine launched the synthetic dye industry, which became the industrial research laboratory, organic chemical manufacture and the first synthetic drugs.
leads.verify: Confirm the dates of Perkin's discovery, patent and first factory production, and how quickly German and Swiss firms took the lead. Check earlier synthetic colourants (picric acid, murexide) so the claim of 'first' is stated precisely.

leads.title: Neodymium-iron-boron magnets in Japan
leads.why: The strongest permanent magnets yet made shrank motors and generators and now sit in hard drives, headphones, electric vehicles and wind turbines.
leads.verify: Confirm Sagawa's sintered magnet and its announcement, and the independent discovery of the same compound by Croat and colleagues at General Motors by rapid solidification, announced at the same 1983 conference. The General Motors work is an independent origin and should probably be a second record.

leads.title: Fibre-tempered pottery in southeastern North America
leads.where: Savannah River valley and the coasts of Georgia, South Carolina and Florida, United States
leads.why: Late Archaic foragers made the first pottery north of Mexico, from which the ceramics of eastern North America descend.
leads.verify: Confirm the earliest dates for Stallings and Orange fibre-tempered wares and the present view on whether they were invented locally or inspired from northern South America. Mesoamerican pottery (Purron, Barra, c. 1900 BCE) is a further case whose independence needs checking.

leads.title: Lead-chamber sulfuric acid in Britain
leads.why: Acid by the ton instead of the bottle became the base chemical of industry, on which bleaching, soda, fertiliser, dye and explosive manufacture all depended.
leads.verify: Confirm Roebuck and Garbett's lead chambers of 1746 and their relation to Joshua Ward's earlier glass-vessel works. Trace the fall in price and the later refinements (Gay-Lussac and Glover towers, the contact process) so links to soda and fertiliser records can be drawn.

leads.title: Glassmaking at Ile-Ife
leads.why: Yoruba glassmakers devised their own high-lime, high-alumina glass from local materials and supplied beads across West Africa, the only known sub-Saharan invention of primary glass.
leads.verify: Confirm the dating of primary glass production at Igbo Olokun and the compositional evidence that the recipe was local and not derived from imported glass. Other regional glass recipes whose independence is debated (lead-barium glass in Warring States China, mineral-soda glass in South India) are candidates for further records.
